body.p: Claims 1 and 3-20 were previously pending. Claims 11-20 were withdrawn from consideration. In this response, claims 1-6 are amended. Therefore, following entry of the present amendments, claims 1 and 3-20 is/are pending.

Applicant's representative Fredrick S. Tsang (Reg. No. 68,680) conducted a telephonicinterview with Examiner Tu on April 29, 2024. During the interview, pending claims 1 and 3-20 and the rejections to those claims under 35 U.S.C. § 103 were discussed. The Examiner agreed that the pending claims appear to be distinguishable over the currently cited references in view of Applicant's arguments, subject to further search and consideration.
The Examiner rejected claims 1, 3, 7, and 10 as obvious over the combination of
Niederkrom et al. (US 2014/0366277), Terawaki et al. (US 2011/0308019), and Bedford (US 4,847,933).

The references do not disclose "the electrically conductive pathways in the top set being configured to be spaced apart from each other to form a top set of horizontal air pathways and the electrically conductive pathways in the bottom set being configured to be spaced apart from each other to form a bottom set of horizontal air pathways," as recited in amended claim 1. At FIG. 3, Niederkrom discloses electrical conductors 126 that form a grid on the same vertical level. As the conductors are on the same vertical level, no top and bottom sets of horizontal air pathways can be formed. Similarly, Terawaki shows longitudinal (01Y, 02Y, ... 10Y) and lateral (01X, 02X, ... 10X) electrodes on the same vertical level at FIG. 3. As the electrodes are
on the same vertical level, no horizontal air pathways can be formed. Bedford does not contain description of the concept of a capacitor or electrically conductive pathways.
The references do not disclose "the top and bottom sets of electrically conductive

pathways separated vertically by an air-permeable dielectric layer that is located between the top and bottom air-permeable substrates," as recited in amended claim 1. Niederkrom recites a compressible dielectric 127 located "between the perpendicular electrical conductors 126 in a middle portion of pressure mat 125." Niederkrom at [0029]. Niederkrom does not disclose, through description or through drawings, electrically conductive pathways separated vertically by an air-permeable dielectric layer. Similarly, Terawaki does not disclose electrically conductive pathways separated vertically by an air-permeable dielectric layer. Bedford does not contain description of the concept of a capacitor or electrically conductive pathways.

The references do not disclose "forming vertical air pathways at a plurality of gaps of the grid, and wherein the dielectric layer and the top and bottom air-permeable substrates comprise cut-outs at the vertical air pathways such that airflow passes vertically through the plurality of gaps of the grid and horizontally through the air-permeable dielectric layer," as recited in amended claim 1. The Office Action states that neither Niederkrom in view of Terawaki does not teach this element. Office Action at 4. At FIG. 1, Bedford recites air channels 23 through layers of a foam support pad, though Bedford does not teach cut-outs at vertical air pathways at gaps of a sensor grid.

In view of the above, claim 1 is patentable over the cited combination of references. Claims 3-10 all depend from claim 1. As such, all arguments made above with reference to claim 1 are equally applicable to these claims. Therefore, these rejections should be withdrawn.

Based on the foregoing, the application is in condition for allowance, and reconsideration of the application is therefore requested. If the Examiner believes that direct contact would help advance prosecution of this application, the Examiner is encouraged to contact the undersigned.
